R7BH-bear-backcountry-0004.name: 3.6 km S of Old Faddy Lake
R7BH-bear-backcountry-0004.pressureWhy: More than 5 km from a drivable road (estimate).

evidence.t: Burn from 2023 (fire R91162), right here: burned areas are spring bear food (90%) and huckleberry grows in old burns (80%) (lessons: Black bear Masterclass 5, Habitat tour).
S facing slope, 11 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Unnamed wetland 90 m S: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

plan: Drive: from Lower Post, about 42 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 59.99831, -129.05375, pull off on pullout (paved road). Map links below.
Walk: 22 km S, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 301 m, about 466 min at 3 km/h.
Camp: flat ground 100 m N of the spot at 767 m (59.80345, -129.07523). Water: unnamed wetland 190 m SE (estimate).

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Aug, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 6-23, Region 6. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2024-12-12, closures 2026-10-16.
